convention_reasoning.the_old_abstention_is_gone: A previous revision of this record reported that the machine ABI record 'abstains from naming a receiver at all (receiver_not_determinable: ecx_read_without_deref)' and listed __stdcall and __thiscall as candidates with confidence UNKNOWN and verdict ABI_UNKNOWN. That is no longer what the record says. The reason it gave -- the body reads ECX without dereferencing it, so a receiver cannot be told from an ordinary register argument -- is still recorded, as abi_derived.receiver.reason = ecx_read_without_deref, and the record determines receiver.present = true anyway, because R1-VFT reasons from the vftable-slot membership instead of from the body's own dereference count. The record's own candidate_conventions is now exactly ["__thiscall"] and its confidence is INFERRED, not UNKNOWN.
convention_reasoning.how_r1_vft_establishes_the_receiver: R1-VFT is the rule the determination names. Its discriminator is a membership fact plus a read fact: the address is a slot of a vptr-backed vftable, and the body READS the register such a dispatch delivers. A COM / __stdcall-shaped body takes its receiver from the first popped stack word and never reads its incoming ECX; this body does read it, at 0x005c8bc0, and that read is what R1-VFT discriminates on. The rule records the result as {receiver_register ECX, receiver_provenance vftable_slot_dispatch, table 0x013f82fc, slot_index 7, cleanup_side callee} and its confidence as INFERRED. INFERRED rather than OBSERVED because nothing in this repository has watched a caller dispatch through the table.
convention_reasoning.how_c6b_names_the_convention: C6B is the rule that named __thiscall, from two facts the record states separately: the callee pops its own stack word, which rules out cdecl and fastcall, and the receiver arrives in ECX. cleanup.bytes = 4 with cleanup.side = callee and cleanup.evidence = "ret 0x4" is confidence OBSERVED, because the immediate is read straight out of the two instruction bytes at 0x005c8be4 (C2 04 00).
convention_reasoning.what_the_convention_does_not_settle: A convention is not an identity. __thiscall says the receiver arrives in ECX; it does not say what the receiver IS. The body copies ECX into EAX, overwrites ECX with the caller's stack word, and never dereferences the incoming value in any register, so the receiver's type, shape, object size, vtable-pointer offset, field, member and layout are all unproven and none is claimed. No owning class is claimed: R1-VFT names ONE table base and the slot's own index, a slot is not a class, and this binary carries no MSVC RTTI. Whether the incoming ECX points at the head of an object or at an interior sub-object is invisible from these twelve instructions, which neither add nor subtract anything, and is carried as an open question.
convention_reasoning.the_stack_word_is_not_the_receiver: The word at entry_ESP+0x4 is an integral 32-bit comparison value and nothing more. It is read once, into ECX, at 0x005c8bc2; it is then compared against three immediates and never again touched. It is never dereferenced, so nothing supports calling it a pointer; it never reaches EAX, so it is not the returned receiver; it is the caller's own pushed slot, so it is not a field of anything this body owns; and no record in this pack gives the three values a name, so calling it an identifier of any kind would be an invention. The model test drives the two values independently and asserts that a compared value sitting in ECX with a non-member on the stack returns zero, so a reconstruction that folded one into the other would be refuted rather than passed.
convention_reasoning.contradiction_noted: A sibling candidate (reconstruction/staging/pkg-palette-classid-slot7/palette_classid_slot7_005c8bc0.hpp) states 'words 0 and 6' of that table hold the thunks. Re-read here, word 6 is 0x005c9070 and disassembles as 56 8b f1 8d 4e 34 (PUSH ESI; MOV ESI,ECX; LEA ECX,[ESI+0x34]) -- an ordinary method prologue, not a thunk. Only word 0 is a this-adjusting thunk. This does not change the conclusion (one adjusting thunk is enough to identify a vtable), and the sibling file was not edited.

mechanics.body_shape: 12 instructions, 39 bytes, no frame, no store, no call, no indirect transfer, no data-segment access. It copies the ECX input into the return register, reads the caller's one stack word into ECX, runs three equality tests against it, and returns the ECX input or zero.

the_three_guards_are_one_membership_test.first: 0x005c8bc6 CMP ECX,0xee3f516e / 0x005c8bcc JZ 0x005c8be4 -- on equality, branch to the shared terminator with EAX still holding the ECX input
the_three_guards_are_one_membership_test.second: 0x005c8bce CMP ECX,0x2f009dd0 / 0x005c8bd4 JZ 0x005c8be4 -- identical in effect
the_three_guards_are_one_membership_test.third: 0x005c8bd6 XOR EDX,EDX / 0x005c8bd8 CMP ECX,0x72deed2b / 0x005c8bde SETNZ DL / 0x005c8be1 DEC EDX / 0x005c8be2 AND EAX,EDX -- SETNZ writes DL against an EDX that XOR has just cleared, so the pair yields 0xffffffff when the argument EQUALS 0x72deed2b and 0 when it does not, which is the same verdict the two JZ guards give
the_three_guards_are_one_membership_test.consequence: the body returns the caller's ECX input when the stack word equals any of the three values, and zero for every other input. The third guard is neither an exception nor an inversion.

mechanics.null_behaviour: A zero stack word matches none of the three, so the fall-through path masks the result to zero whatever the ECX input is. A zero ECX input returns zero on every input, membership or not, because the return word is the input and the mask is applied to it.

mechanics.byte_level_confirmation_2026_09_29: Re-read first-hand from the live bridge, independent of the pack, and decoded by hand. /read_memory @ 0x005c8bc0, 39 bytes, hex 8bc18b4c240481f96e513fee741681f9d09d002f740e33d281f92bedde720f95c24a23c2c20400 decodes instruction for instruction to the twelve lines above: 8b c1 MOV EAX,ECX | 8b 4c 24 04 MOV ECX,[ESP+0x4] (SIB, disp8 0x04) | 81 f9 6e 51 3f ee CMP ECX,0xee3f516e | 74 16 JZ +0x16, i.e. 0x005c8bce+0x16 = 0x005c8be4 | 81 f9 d0 9d 00 2f CMP ECX,0x2f009dd0 | 74 0e JZ +0x0e, i.e. 0x005c8bd6+0x0e = 0x005c8be4 | 33 d2 XOR EDX,EDX | 81 f9 2b ed de 72 CMP ECX,0x72deed2b | 0f 95 c2 SETNZ DL (opcode 0f 90+cc, cc=0x02; mod=11, reg field 010 = EDX, r/m field 000 = DL) | 4a DEC EDX | 23 c2 AND EAX,EDX (mod=11, reg=EAX, r/m=EDX -- a full 32-bit word AND, not a byte operation) | c2 04 00 RET 0x4. Both JZ displacements are confirmed to land on the shared terminator 0x005c8be4 by arithmetic on the byte offsets, and the body is 39 bytes with no padding, matching Ghidra's body_end 0x005c8be6. Also re-read first-hand: the eight words at 0x013f82fc are 0x005c9060, 0x00c6fb40, 0x0076ded0, 0x004535b0, 0x00c6a960, 0x007b86e0, 0x005c9070, 0x005c8bc0, so word 7 is this function and the reported xref at 0x013f8318 is that word (0x013f82fc + 7*4 = 0x013f8318). The bytes at 0x005c9060 are 83 e9 04 e9 08 00 00 00, i.e. SUB ECX,0x4 then JMP rel32 +8 from 0x005c906a to 0x005c9072 -- an MSVC this-adjusting thunk, which corroborates the convention_reasoning below. Ghidra holds no function at 0x005c9060, which is consistent with the repo's standing note that vtable detection never ran on this binary.

return_semantics.value: the caller's ECX input, all 32 bits, when the stack word equals one of the three compared values; zero otherwise
return_semantics.width: 4 bytes on every path. 0x005c8bc0 is the only write to EAX before either JZ and neither JZ touches it, so the pass-through paths return the input bit for bit; the fall-through path is a full-word AND, so it returns either the same word or zero.
return_semantics.disagreement_not_resolved: Live decompilation spells the return bool and tests only the low byte of ECX. A bool is a statement about the first byte; the machine returns the whole register. Ghidra's own comment on that function records 'Unknown calling convention' and its prototype (six parameters) is contradicted by the body's RET 0x4, so its rendering is not treated as an oracle. The record's return_semantics is unclassified_in_EAX with register_class aggregate_unknown. This package declares the record's own name for that word and narrows nothing.
return_semantics.ownership: The body acquires and releases nothing. It performs no reference counting, no allocation and no transfer of ownership: it either hands back the caller's own ECX input unchanged or hands back zero.
return_semantics.lifetime: The returned word on a membership path is bit-identical to the value the caller left in ECX, so its lifetime is entirely the caller's. On the masked path the value is zero, which owns nothing. Nothing here extends or shortens any lifetime, and whether a caller treats the word as a pointer is not established: the pack records zero callers.

a zero ECX input returns zero on a membership case, separating 'returns the word' from 'returns a non-null word'

off-by-one in either direction for all three values returns zero, as do values matching only a low byte, only a low half word, or a high half word of one -- so the comparisons are full 32-bit equalities
a compared value sitting in ECX with a non-member on the stack returns zero, so the three constants are tested against the STACK word and the receiver and the message-id word stay rigorously separate

a hand-written x86-32 assembly caller (four words pushed, three of them fillers) records ESP after the frame reservation and immediately after the call returns, and asserts the callee dropped exactly the RET immediate decoded out of the image bytes. A wrong arity yields a different delta (sixteen for a bare RET, eight for a second stack word, four for a third) rather than a crash, and the expected delta is computed rather than written as a literal.

survivors.proof_of_indistinguishability: This is a PURE permutation, not a behaviour change, and it is the one mutation in this set that no black-box check over this interface can kill. All three membership paths return the same word, so the return value is a function of set membership in {0xee3f516e, 0x2f009dd0, 0x72deed2b} alone, and a permutation of the guard order does not change that set. The surviving mutant is therefore identical to the original from the caller's side on every point of the 32-bit input space, under both cleanup sides and every observed register. The machine's arrangement is recovered from the listing, and it is recorded in the per-instruction annotations of dfw_005c8bc0.cpp and in the decoded-byte checks above (the JZ displacements and the SETNZ/DEC bytes are read out of kTargetBytes and pinned), not by claiming a behavioural check that covers it. The same argument covers writing the membership test as one expression instead of three comparisons.

known_limitations: The three compared values are read as raw words. A reconstruction that tested the same three numbers through a different mechanism (a table lookup, a computed jump) would be indistinguishable here, since the interface is a return word.

Nothing here observes the body's internal register allocation beyond what the machine's own bytes pin: the model is asserted through its return word, its stack discipline, and a transcription of the thirty-nine bytes, not through a byte-for-byte recompilation of the reconstructed entry (which is an ordinary declarable C++ function here, not a naked transcription).

The probe checks that the callee dropped the RET immediate the bytes carry, but not the reverse direction: a callee that popped MORE than the caller pushed would destroy the return address, and that is reported as a crash rather than as a failed check. The M10 mutation (a second stack word) is caught on the near side, which is the side that can be observed.
mutation_report.note_on_M9_and_M10: Mutating the convention macro or the arity in the .cpp alone does not build, because the declaration in the header and the definition in the .cpp would then disagree. That is a link-time shape, not a behavioural result, so both mutations are applied to both files and are scored on the run. They are the two mutations the hand-written assembly caller was written to catch, and both are caught.

model_test.probe_register_discipline: The hand-written x86-32 probe touches ONLY caller-saved registers -- EAX, ECX and EDX -- and keeps every sample in its own %ebp frame. It never writes ESI, EDI or EBX: each is callee-saved, so a probe that borrows one corrupts its CALLER rather than itself, and on a PIC i386 build EBX additionally holds the GOT base, so taking it over inside inline assembly invalidates every address the compiler forms around the block. EBP is used only as the frame pointer the probe pushes and pops itself, and the epilogue restores ESP from %ebp rather than by arithmetic on the number of bytes a callee happened to drop. The block is a top-level assembly definition of a real function symbol, so it is emitted as a function of its own and never inlined.
model_test.no_tautology: No check in this test compares a value with its own copy of itself. Every comparison is against something independently derived: the three compared values and the RET immediate are DECODED at run time out of kTargetBytes -- the target's own thirty-nine bytes as transcribed from GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x005c8bc0 -- by scanning for the 81 F9 CMP opcode pair and reading the little-endian imm32 that follows it, and by reading the imm16 of the C2 RET; the scan is required to find exactly three CMPs. The expected ESP delta in the stack-discipline check is computed from the four words the probe pushes and from that decoded RET immediate, not written as a literal. The two JZ targets are decoded from the same bytes and required to land on the address of the RET. The header's transcribed ABI data (convention verdict, confidence, candidate count, ambiguity count, receiver register, receiver provenance, cleanup side, receiver-present, bounds-only, dereference count, field-offset-claimed) is compared against literals written in the test, transcribed from the machine record. The header's three named constants are compared against the decoded bytes, and its published CMP offsets against the offsets the scan finds.

conditions: The original process reaches 0x005c8bc0 with a receiver in ECX, which needs a vtable-detection pass or an SDK header to arrange: this pack records zero callers and the address is reachable only as vtable word 7.
Both inputs are captured: the ECX word at entry and the stack word at entry_ESP+0x4, together with the returned EAX.

The captured stack words include one equal to each of 0xee3f516e, 0x2f009dd0 and 0x72deed2b, and at least one equal to none of them -- otherwise the return word is zero on every sample and the membership test is not exercised.
The returned EAX is compared against the reconstructed signature, and specifically checked for its full 32 bits rather than truncated to a flag, which is the one claim the static machine contradicts.

The value consumed from the slot at 0x013f8318 is observed at a real dispatch. That would raise the convention and receiver determination from INFERRED to OBSERVED; it is not needed to make the determination, which R1-VFT and C6B already make.

unresolved_questions: Is the SDK name right? A 12-instruction leaf that makes no call, touches no global and performs no I/O is not the shape of a resource-loading body. The name comes from the SDK symbol table's address binding, not from a caller in this binary -- the pack records fan_in 0 -- and nothing here either supports or refutes it.

Why do a six-parameter SDK prototype and a RET 0x4 body sit at the same address? Either the SDK address binding, the SDK header, or the shipped binary is wrong. This record does not decide which, and it decides what the function is called. The ABI determination does not touch this: __thiscall and a six-parameter prototype disagree about the stack, not about the convention, and the machine's own cleanup evidence (four bytes) is what fixes the argument count at one.

What are 0xee3f516e, 0x2f009dd0 and 0x72deed2b? Two of them leave the result untouched and the third forces zero, which together make one membership test. Nothing in this body, in any callee (there are none) or in any global says what any of them is. A sibling candidate reports an SDK ENUM_ENTRY value match that would name them Object, UTFWin::IWinProc and Palettes::PalettePageUI; the SDK clone is absent from this machine, so the match was not re-derived here and no SDK name is used in this package. A base type, a windowing interface and a palette UI have no domain in common, so the reading does not form a coherent predicate even if the match is right -- which is a reason to keep it out of the model until it is re-derived from a build-matched table.

Why does one virtual slot test exactly these three values? A cast or query helper would normally test a small set of interfaces a specific class implements. Either the slot has a narrower purpose than a class-id query, or the class-id names in the SDK are not what this body compares. Not claimed either way.

What consumes the returned word? The body hands back the caller's ECX input or zero, which reads as a cast/query result, but no caller of this address exists in the pack (xref_count is 1 and it is vtable slot 7, not a call), so nothing here shows whether the word is tested for null, truncated, or stored as a pointer.

Is the return contract a bool? Live decompilation says bool and the machine returns all four bytes of the register it was given, unmodified, on both pass-through paths. The record classifies the return as unclassified_in_EAX with register_class aggregate_unknown and type null. This package declares the width and disclaims the meaning; the bool reading is not adopted and not refuted here.

Which class owns the vtable at 0x013f82fc, and what is the member called? It is a vtable -- word 0 is an MSVC this-adjusting thunk at 0x005c9060, read live -- and word 7 is this function, but the only name near it in .rdata is the string 'paletteItemUIClassId' and nothing read here proves the table belongs to that class. No owning class, no slot member name and no vtable identity are claimed, and none can be: this binary has no MSVC RTTI and no vtable-detection pass has ever run on it.

What IS the receiver? The machine determines that a receiver arrives in ECX (R1-VFT, on the vftable-slot membership) and C6B names __thiscall from that plus the callee-side cleanup, both at confidence INFERRED. It determines nothing about what the receiver is: the body copies ECX into EAX at 0x005c8bc0, overwrites ECX with the stack word at 0x005c8bc2, and never dereferences the incoming value in any register. So its type, shape, object size, vtable-pointer offset, field, member and layout are all unproven, and no field offset is claimed in either direction. Whether the incoming ECX points at the head of an object or at an interior sub-object is invisible from these twelve instructions, which neither add nor subtract anything.

Is the receiver's identity settled? R1-VFT establishes the receiver from the slot membership at 0x013f82fc, and the record's own receiver.reason = ecx_read_without_deref records that the BODY alone could not have established it. Those are two different questions and both are recorded; neither is re-litigated here. Raising the determination from INFERRED to OBSERVED needs a real dispatch through the table, which this pack does not contain.

Is there a caller anywhere? The pack records no call edge into this address, only the data reference from 0x013f8318, so the modelled argument surface is what the body reads, not what any known caller passes.

Is the stack word a message id? The listing says what it is used for -- three 32-bit equality comparisons against three immediates, and nothing else -- and this package claims exactly that. The word's role in the original (a message id, a class id, an interface token, an index, a flag word) is not established by anything in this body, in any callee (there are none) or in any global, so the model calls it an integral comparison value and no more. Naming it would be an invention, and a sibling SDK value match that would name the three values could not be re-derived on this machine.
